answer:
Keep them as two specimens, and put the continuity where it actually lives — in the rock body the two crews drilled into, and in an attributed inference — not in the identity of the two boxes. Both 1968 accession numbers stay in the record permanently, and the old loan paperwork needs no change at all.

1. What each boxed segment is. Model each accessioned segment with multiple instantiation as E19 Physical Object and S13 Sample (CRMsci). S13 is unusually well aimed at this case: its parent S11 Amount of Matter says in so many words that subclasses may define very different identity conditions for the integrity of the content, 'such as chemical composition, or the sequence of layers of a bore core', and S13 says a sample ceases to exist when the representative qualities become corrupted, giving 'the layering of a bore core' as its example. That is exactly the property the stratigrapher is reading. You need the E19 aspect as well, because custody runs on E18: P30 transferred custody of has range E18, and S13 is not an E18 (S13 < S11 < S10 Material Substantial, and S10 is a *superclass* of E18, not a subclass), so a bare S13 cannot be the object of a loan. Multiple instantiation is what CRMsci itself prescribes here: S1 Matter Removal and S2 Sample Taking both say the removed matter 'may acquire a persistent identity of different nature beyond the act of its removal, such as becoming a physical object in the narrower sense', to be modelled by multiple instantiation.

2. Why two and not one. Identity in the CRM is not read off matter. What individuates the two segments is that each was brought out of the ground by its own S2 Sample Taking, with its own O4 sampled at place — the two boreholes are 40 m apart, so the two removals are at different places by construction. Martin Doerr's line in the S11 thread is the relevant principle: the 'sampleness' of a split sample 'goes back to the initial removal'. Nothing physical has happened since 1968 to make one thing out of the two. The CRM has explicit machinery for one-becomes-two (S24 Sample Splitting with O27 split and O29 removed sub-sample; E80 Part Removal, whose scope note is expressly 'a basis for reasoning about the history, and continuity of identity over time, of objects that are removed from other objects') and for two-becomes-one (E79 Part Addition, or E81 Transformation where the originals cease to exist) — but every one of these is an *event*. A stratigrapher re-reading fifty-year-old logs is not one of them. Declaring the two segments to be one specimen would assert a joining that never took place. Note also that connect E19 E19 offers nothing for 'was once physically continuous with': only P46 is composed of (which requires the part's spatial extent to be included in the whole's, and is transitive and asymmetric), P198 holds or supports, P130 shows features of and CRMdig's L54. The absence is informative — in the CRM this kind of link runs through the source body or through an event.

3. The CRM will not decide identity for you, but two of its rules push this way. The SIG's settled position is that identity criteria are the modeller's to declare: 'It is task of each type of E18 to define its own identity conditions' and 'There is no natural identity to something material'. Formally, then, the survey may define its specimen concept as it likes — but two constraints bear on it. (a) E10 Transfer of Custody's scope note says physical possession 'requires that the object of custody be in the hands of the keeper at least with a part representative for the whole', and that the way a representative part is defined 'should ensure that it is unambiguous who keeps a part and who the whole and should be consistent with the identity criteria of the kept instance of E18 Physical Thing'. Two boxes, two buildings, two keepers, fifty years of separate loans: merged into one specimen, every custody and location statement becomes ambiguous, and the KB ends with one object in two places at once — the exact failure Doerr warns about in t0891. (b) E10 also states that the museum notion of accession differs between institutions, that the CRM therefore models legal ownership and physical custody separately, and that institutions model their own notions of accession from those parts; and E19's scope note says the decision as to what is documented as a complete item rather than by its parts 'may be purely administrative or may be a result of the order in which the item was acquired'. The accessioned segment is a legitimate documentation unit precisely because it was accessioned.

4. Where the continuity goes. The thing that is continuous is the rock, not the boxes. Model the drilled body as A2 Stratigraphic Volume Unit (CRMarchaeo) — A2 covers connected portions of terrain 'on, in, or under the surface of earth or seafloor', and AP11's scope note explicitly covers physical relationships 'found between stratigraphic units in archaeological or geological documentation', including 'earthquake induced faults'. Then: each S2 Sample Taking O3 sampled from the unit, O4 sampled at the borehole position, O5 removed the S13 Sample. If the stratigrapher's claim is that both crews cut the same unit, express it by having both sampling events O3 sampled from one A2 instance — that is the 'single identity' the case is groping for, asserted at the level where it is true. If the two logs are kept as two units, relate them with AP11 has physical relation to, typed via AP11.1 has type ('continuous with', 'faulted against'); the fault surface itself, if needed, is an A3 Stratigraphic Interface. Either way the boxed segments stay two.

5. Record the claim as a claim. The stratigrapher 'believes' — so do not bake it into identity, where it cannot be withdrawn. Use I5 Inference Making (CRMinf, a subclass of I1 Argumentation) P14 carried out by the stratigrapher, P16 used specific object / P17 was motivated by the 1968 logs (E31 Document), J2 concluded that an I2 Belief, J4 that an I4 Proposition Set holding the continuity proposition, J5 holds to be an I6 Belief Value such as 'probable' (I4 and I6 come along only as the ranges of J4 and J5). This is the pattern the reference document recommends under 'Modelling principles > Authorship of Knowledge Base Contents' for statements that carry a responsibility. If the repository writes the claim into its own catalogue on the stratigrapher's authority, that act is I7 Belief Adoption.

6. The loan records: honour both numbers, and change nothing. Neither choice licenses rewriting them. Each 1968 accession number is an E42 Identifier, and P1 is identified by is a shortcut for the path E1 . P140i was attributed by : E15 Identifier Assignment . P37 assigned : E42 Identifier (connect prints this full path), so model the two 1968 numberings as two E15 Identifier Assignment events, each P14 carried out by its own crew or repository, each P37 assigning its own number. Both remain asserted forever. The loans are E10 Transfer of Custody, P30 transferred custody of the individual segment; the paperwork is E31 Document, P70 documents the loan event and P67 refers to the identifier it cites. Those documents are historical propositions about what was lent under which number, and 'Modelling principles > Monotonicity' means correct old statements are never withdrawn, only added to. Do not use P38 deassigned here. P38's scope note is precisely on point — deassignment 'may be necessary when an item is taken out of an inventory, a new numbering system is introduced or items are merged or split up' — which means that IF the survey ever physically joins the segments and issues one number, the correct record is a new, dated E15 Identifier Assignment that P37 assigns the new identifier and P38 deassigns the two old ones. Even then the old loan records stay valid, because the deassignment is an event with a time-span and an actor, not an erasure. Until then, if a single citable handle is wanted, use P48 has preferred identifier (many-to-one) for it, or better, per P48's own note, type the relevant E15 Identifier Assignment as the preferred one; both original numbers remain reachable through P1.

7. Two things to avoid. Do not reach for L54 is same as (CRMdig) between the two segments: its definition is 'a non-unique identification', and using it would assert the very identity that is in doubt while hiding whose opinion it is. And note that CRMbase deliberately has no co-reference construct to lean on — E91 Co-Reference Assignment and P155 were withdrawn from the CRM 6.1 text under Issue 230 (Oxford, February 2015) and handed to CRMinf — which is a second reason the claim belongs in an I2 Belief.

8. If they want one record for the reconstructed section. E19's scope note does admit aggregates 'made for functional purposes of whatever kind, independent of physical coherence', so a third E19 with its own identifier, holding the two segments as P46 parts, is available — not E78 Curated Holding, which its scope note reserves for curated aggregations under a collection development plan and explicitly says collective objects forming wholes should be E19 instead. Be aware this is a strained use of P46 while the boxes are in different buildings, since P46 requires the part's spatial extent to be included in the whole's (its FOL entails P132 spatiotemporal overlap); it becomes clean only if the segments are actually brought together on one shelf. In every version, the two accessioned segments keep their own identities and their own numbers.

rejected_alternatives.option: One merged specimen (a single E19/S13 with the two boxes as its parts, via P46 is composed of)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: P46 requires the part's spatial extent to be included in the whole's and its FOL entails P132 spatiotemporal overlap, which two boxes in two buildings do not satisfy; and merging would break E10 Transfer of Custody's requirement that it be unambiguous who keeps a part and who the whole, leaving the KB with one specimen in two locations under two keepers.

rejected_alternatives.option: E79 Part Addition (or E81 Transformation) to make the two into one whole
rejected_alternatives.why_not: These are physical events. Nobody has joined the segments; the only new thing is a stratigrapher's reading of old logs. Instantiating either would assert an activity that never happened.

rejected_alternatives.option: S24 Sample Splitting with O27 split / O29 removed sub-sample
rejected_alternatives.why_not: This is CRMsci's machinery for one sample becoming several, and it is the wrong direction: the two segments were never one accessioned sample that got split. Its absence of a mirror image is the point — samples are individuated by their removal, and CRMsci offers no merge event.

rejected_alternatives.option: P38 deassigned, to retire one of the two 1968 accession numbers
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Its scope note reserves deassignment for items 'taken out of an inventory', a new numbering system, or items 'merged or split up'. None has occurred: both segments still exist as separate custody units. Deassigning would also strand the loan paperwork that cites the number.

rejected_alternatives.option: L54 is same as (CRMdig) between the two segments
rejected_alternatives.why_not: It is defined as 'a non-unique identification' with no place for whose opinion it is or when it was formed; it would assert the disputed identity as bare data instead of as the stratigrapher's I2 Belief.
Not available: withdrawn from the CIDOC CRM text at version 6.1 under Issue 230 (Oxford, February 2015) and referred to CRMinf, so there is no CRMbase co-reference construct to use.

rejected_alternatives.option: E78 Curated Holding for a single 'reunited section' record
rejected_alternatives.why_not: E78 is for aggregations assembled under a collection development plan, and its scope note explicitly says collective objects that form wholes should be documented as E19 Physical Object rather than E78.

rejected_alternatives.option: S3 Measurement by Sampling for the 1968 coring
rejected_alternatives.why_not: S3 covers sampling where the sample 'is typically not identified and preserved beyond the context of this activity'. These cores were accessioned, numbered and kept for fifty years, so the sample must be identified and preserved: plain S2 Sample Taking with O5 removed.

siblings_considered.why_not: E26 Physical Feature is for features 'physically attached in an integral way' to surrounding matter; that fits the rock while it was still in the ground, but a core lifted into a box has objective physical boundaries and is movable, i.e. a unit for documentation — E19.

S12 Amount of Fluid is the other subclass of S11, for gases and liquids identified by being kept in a container. A rock core is solid, and its identity criterion is the sequence of its layers, which is what S13's scope note names.

E80 Part Removal (the other subclass of S1 Matter Removal) frames the act as diminishing a whole by detaching a part of it — apt for deaccessioning or dismantling an object. Here matter was taken to be representative of the formation for analysis, which is what S2 Sample Taking means, and only S2 carries O3 sampled from / O4 sampled at / O5 removed.

A3 Stratigraphic Interface is a boundary surface, and the fault itself would indeed be one. But what was cored and what the stratigrapher matched is a volume of rock, not a surface, so the sampled unit is A2 Stratigraphic Volume Unit; A3 stays available for the fault plane.

S27 Observation (a sibling under I1 Argumentation) is for knowledge gained from empirical evidence at a place and time. Nobody observed the two segments as continuous; the continuity is inferred from old logs, which is I5 Inference Making.

E3 Condition State (a sibling under E2 Temporal Entity) is a period during which a physical thing is in a certain material state. The thing being asserted here is not a state of the rock but an actor's holding of a proposition to be true, which is I2 Belief.

E17 Type Assignment would classify the segments (e.g. as belonging to a formation) rather than name them. The 1968 numbers are identifiers, so the assignment act is E15 with P37 assigned; a later opinion about continuity is not an identifier assignment either.

E35 Title is the closest sibling under E41 Appellation but is not a plausible rival: accession numbers are codes assigned for unique identification within an organisation, not culturally recognisable titles. I am naming it as the nearest thing rather than as a real contender.

E8 Acquisition transfers legal ownership. A loan moves physical custody only, and E10's scope note is explicit that the CRM models ownership and custody separately — the loan paperwork records custody, and using E8 would misstate the survey's title as having changed.

E33 Linguistic Object captures the paperwork as text in a language. What matters is that these records make propositions about the loans and the numbered segments, i.e. P70 documents and P67 refers to — that is E31 Document. Multiple instantiation with E33 is harmless but adds nothing here.

notes: Three tool frictions. (1) `concept S24` returns 'No such concept', even though S2's dossier lists S24 among its subclasses and O27 split / O29 removed sub-sample both declare S24 Sample Splitting as their domain; I could only reach S24 Sample Splitting through those two property dossiers. (2) CRMsci S5 Inference Making and CRMinf I5 Inference Making carry near-identical scope notes and both declare I1 Argumentation as parent, but I1's own dossier lists I5 (not S5) among its subclasses, so the two labels are not reconciled in the index. I proposed I5 to keep the belief chain (I2/I4/I6, J2/J4/J5) inside CRMinf; S5 would serve equally. (3) `concept O29` attached an episode about 'Renaming O29 Observable Proposition', which looks like an id collision between models rather than a discussion of O29 removed sub-sample, so I did not use it. Substantive residue: the CRM offers no property meaning 'was once physically continuous with' between two removed specimens (connect E19 E19 and connect S13 S13 return only part-whole, containment, P130 and CRMdig L54), and the S11 thread ends with Doerr saying a transitive property of its own is probably needed for split samples, with no resolution I could find. That gap is why the recommendation routes the continuity through the sampled A2 unit and an I2 Belief rather than through a direct link between the boxes. Also, the case says the two segments are 'physically continuous' although the boreholes are 40 m apart; O4 sampled at forces the two removals to two distinct places, which is itself the argument that the continuity is a property of the formation, not of the two amounts of matter.
